_about: Tool-usability eval scenarios. Each entry: a natural-language `task`, the `expected_tools` the deterministic discovery layer (help(goal=...) / intents.match_intents) should surface, a `group` (Create|Edit|Inspect|Export|Live), and `out_of_scope` for asks the server must REFUSE to map. An expected tool is written `tool:op` — `edit:create_rect`, `open:canvas`, `inspect:objects`, `export:profile`, `live_edit:apply` — where `op` is the edit op, the open source mode, the inspect section, the export target kind, or the render/history/live/actions/help `target`/`action`/`topic`; a bare `tool` is covered by any op of that tool. Scoring (evals/run_eval.py): a scenario is a HIT when at least one expected entry is among the targets help(goal=...) returns (or, for out_of_scope=true, when it flags the task out_of_scope with no matches). This evaluates the server's OWN deterministic discovery surface — NO live LLM. A future real-agent runner can consume the same schema (swap the runner; keep task/expected_tools/group/out_of_scope).
